Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Just why do young women choose to lock themselves away from society and devote themselves to God? Journeyman.special.

Unique Selling Point:

Script:


Transcript

Title: Breaking Silence

Programme: SUNDAY

Broadcaster: TVNZ

Reporter & Cameraman: Chris Cooke

Editor: Paul Anderson

Executive Producer: Max Adams

Duration: 13:02 (Including Intro)


Intro:

Now.. a special story. Rare access inside the Carmelite Monastery in Christchurch.

Women, nuns, separated from the world and their families behind high walls.

Hours of silence and prayer. A life of poverty, chastity and obedience.

It's another world and after 10 years of consideration they agreed to talk openly about their lives to

Sunday producer Chris Cooke.

They asked however that he enter the Monastery alone.


FX: Birds, bells tolling and singing

Sister Catherine IV

When I was younger I would never have seen myself as a nun.
Ever, ever, ever, ever.

I was Catherine Smith and now I am Sister Catherine of Christ a Carmelite Novice.

I have been here since 2014.

I became a Catholic when I was 18 years old.

I felt God ask me to be here. A mysterious call to a life of prayer for others.

There was some fear. Can I live the life?

Sister Cushla IV

My name is sister Cushla.

I'm called the novice mistress.

FX “Glory be to the Father.”
Sister Cushla IV continued:

I provide academic formation.

And I need to present the demands of the life.

Sister Cushla to Sister Catherine

FX "We are shaping ourselves to his way of living”.

Sister Cushla IV

As we are following Christ who was poor, chaste and obedient

So we're actually trying to live an imitation of him.

When I was a teenager I really wanted to marry and have a large family, that was my dream.

I came to do a school project on the Carmelites. There was something that attracted me about them. But also something about the whole idea that repulsed me.

I took away the, the pamphlets //and over the years I developed this love hate relationship with them,

FX Prayer Session "Pray for us, pray for us”

Sister Dorothea IV - (Prioress of the Monastery)

We see prayer as being as embracing the whole world. And to me embracing the world was a, was a really big thing for me.

My name is sister Dorothea Wilkes Prioress of this Carmelite monastery.

It was the last thing in the whole world I would have expected to be here.

I was 28 when I entered the monastery and I had a very full life.
Perhaps the best and the worst of life.

I was living a sort of hippie life.

Because I didn't believe in God at all, I thought Christians were really soft in the head. I couldn't bear Christians.

Sister Dorothea IV Continued.

I had a huge experience of god when I was 19.

that turned my life around overnight.

It was at a huge rock concert/ .

A Black Sabbath rock concert up in Ngaruawahia.

The music was pounding into me.

There as a cross burning on the hill.

I started to see all my life going in front of my eyes.

I knew that there was something not quite true in that life. There's not something true in drugs, there's not something true in relationships that are not, are not wholly pure relationships/.

I didn't want to do this anymore.

So that' when I started to set my sights on the contemplative life to pray for others, that they would be also liberated from the things that were binding me to living a life that was not a happy life.

Sister Catherine IV

People might think that you have to be a pure catholic virgin to be able to become a nun.
That's not how God works. It is not the Carmelites who determines who comes,
God determines who comes and who is called.

In Carmel we begin our day with prayer at 6am.

Getting up early every day is challenging especially in Winter

Sister Cushla IV

It's our first time of prayer which we have 7 times a day.

All during the day the bells ring to call us to prayer.

Then we have the 2 silent hours of prayer.

Sister Dorothea IV

God talks in silences. He, He's, there's an amazing depth to that silence.

You just love to be in the silence.

FX Phone ring ring

Sister Dorothea IV

We're involved with/ people ringing for prayer ringing writing.

Always asking for intercessory prayer. That's one of our biggest works you might say is
replying to those people and praying for them.

Sister Cushla IV

I believe that our prayer here does have an impact on the outside. We have to live by faith because we usually don't see the results of our prayer.

Sister Catherine IV

What defines monastic life for us is the separation from the world which would be symbolised by the physical wall that we have around our monastery.

It is also the grills that we have in our chapel separating us from the public.


Off camera Question

So the public can't see you at all?

Sister Catherine IV

No

Off camera Question

You're hidden?

Sister Catherine IV

We're hidden.

Sister Cushla IV

We usually only see our family and friends once a month

Fx "hello! how are you"

I can't hug them, yeah that's right, but we weren't actually big huggers (laughter) in our family anyway.

Most of my family are not Catholic, so it was a huge thing for them to take on.

Sister Dorothea IV

The big thing was leaving the family.

That was the hardest reality.

They're not Catholic so you can imagine that wasn't easy for them.

Sister Catherine IV

I was raised Presbyterian. My father is a Presbyterian Minister. He is now retired.

It doesn't make any sense to them.

Especially that I miss out on family events.

When I first came I saw the wall of the monastery and was rather intimidated.

Excited but a bit nervous. What have I got myself into! I was greeted with open arms.

when the door closed behind me I felt like I was in another planet!

A while later when I first walked into the room to dress me in the habit there was two pairs of scissors. And that is the first time I realised that my hair was going to be cut, which took me by surprise a little bit but I wasn't worried.

Sister Catherine IV contd...

That symbolises a letting go of any attachments I have to impressing others.

A letting go of myself in a way.

From the moment of receiving the habit I felt very at peace. And that peace surprised me and that peace hasn't left me.

It was very moving.

Until I make my solemn vows I wear this white for about 5 years.

Taking the final vows the solemn vows in the monastery for me would mean that I am completely dedicating myself to god and this way of life forever.

And as far as I can tell I will, but, gods will be done.

Off camera question

So you may not stay?

Sister Catherine IV

I may not.

Graphic: Coming Up...

Off camera question

What do you give up to be here?

Sister Catherine IV

The deep friendship that can exist between a man and a woman. You give up that for the sake of god.

Off camera question

Is that something you think about?

Sister Catherine IV

Yes

END PART ONE

----

PART TWO

FX BELL & Sisters chanting, “Lord hear my voice”

Sister Cushla IV

It becomes a, a kind of a gentle rhythm throughout the day,
of coming to prayer of getting into our work.

FX Music Hallelujah, Hallelujah.


Sister Cushla IV

I found it rather exhausting to begin with.

On a Saturday you seem to clean the whole monastery.

We've got gardens and we have got orchards, and they supply a lot of what we need.

Sister Catherine IV

Our Steers/ they help keep the grass down.

I enjoy coming out here I am often out here just by myself.

It's a different means of thinking of god and being with him and being grateful for what he gives us and how he provides for us.

Sister Catherine IV

We make the altar breads for many of the parishes in Christchurch

We sell them and they are a bit of income for us

They are the body of christ which are consecrated in the mass

The priest distributes them in communion

FX Priest "Sister the body of Christ"

Sister Cushla IV

Confession is available to us once a week

Fx "In the name of the father and the son.."

Yes every week (laughter). Yes we actually, we don't run out of things!

FX Bell ringing./Chanting

Sister Catherine IV

We are vegetarians The first Carmelites gave up meat as a way to be poor.

Sister Cushla IV

Most of our day is spent in silence. And so we come together and we talk.

Sister Catherine IV

Two times a day of recreation for an hour.

It’s a very joyful time.

It is very rejuvenating.


Sister Dorothea IV

That gives us strength to go back into that silence again.

Sister Catherine IV

I come here many times during the day.

It is the one place in the monastery that is reserved just for me.

We are not just nuns but hermits

So this is the place where I try and live that out

Sister Dorothea IV

It’s like a desert inside.

We don't have the newspapers, we don't have TV . We don't watch the news

You are Very much emptied of images and of things that, that would clutter up your life from a life of prayer.

OFF CAMERA QUESTION

Were you aware of the issue/ of the sexual abuse of people within the Catholic Church?

Sister Dorothea IV

Abuse? Oh ah well aware of it. Ah oh I think that's been one of the biggest swords in our side for a long time. To think that would even be happening it was just so, it's just beyond our ken, it is just unreal.

It's an issue that just makes our heart bleed it is horrible

Sister Catherine IV

We have three hermitages on the property.

We have our monthly retreat of one day and
ten days once a year when we separate ourselves to be entirely alone with god.

Off Camera Question

So not only silence, extra silence?

Sister Catherine IV

Yes (laughter) yes

Sister Dorothea IV

Have I ever questioned the sacrifice I've made? Not exactly questioned them but I've certainly felt the desire for those things that I've left.

We give up/being able to have a family, being able to have your own husband.

You can still have those longings. We're still, we're women and we've got many womanly, womanly instincts and needs.

if we know ourselves and we know why we've given it up then it's easy to work through those things.

Sister Cushla IV

All those things that I wanted from a husband, and believed I would get from husband, I get it in a much deeper much more spiritual way from Jesus Christ.

Off camera question

Through prayer?

Sister Cushla IV

Through prayer/

Sister Catherine IV

You give up the possibility of a career. Tthe possibility of a life, A committed relationship with a man.

The joys that come with that. The pleasures that come with that.

Off camera question

Is that something you think about?

Yes

Off camera question

Is it hard?

Sister Catherine IV

It has its hard moments

I feel sometimes the desire to be in the arms of a man.

But not in the sense of longing for something I can't have or don't have, just pondering the mystery of why me. Why has god called me and why has he put in my heart this desire that he is fulfilling in abundance.

Off camera question

Do you ever consider that if there is no heaven the incredible sacrifice you will have made with your life?

Sister Dorothea IV

You're quite right, if there's no heaven we've made an enormous sacrifice. In fact I've said, sometimes said to people if there's no heaven I'd be over this wall in two minutes, I'd be out of here It's only for the sake of, of our eternal life.

I know that this is where I am myself, this is where I can feel totally who I am. And that to me is, is, is everything.

END

--------------------
Back announce: So in a few Months sister Catherine is to decide if she will take the next step towards here vows. We will keep you posted.
